(Two students are talking on the street.)
Teng Fei: Hi, I’m Teng Fei. It’s my first time to come here.
Liu Qiang: Hi, Teng Fei. I’m Liu Qiang. (21)
Teng Fei: Glad to meet you, too! Is there a science and technology museum nearby?
Liu Qiang: (22)
Teng Fei: I heard we can see the scenes of the first men landing on the Moon there.
Liu Qiang: Exactly. You can also know about China’s space exploration.
Teng Fei: Cool! (23)

Teng Fei: I see. (24)

sections.title: 无声的父爱
sections.passage:
Peter’s father was a man of few words. He (26) had a heart-to-heart talk with Peter. He was busy with his work and usually got home very late. How Peter (27) his father could play basketball or go fishing with him!
One evening, while working on a math problem, Peter found it so difficult that he wanted to (28). He was about to close the book when a small yellow note fell out (29). On it was a short message with a lovely hand-drawn heart. It said, “You can do it! — Dad”.
Peter felt (30). Soon he found another note in his English dictionary, and one more in his favorite magazine. (31) he saw those notes written in his father’s beautiful handwriting, he was lost in thought.
Peter looked towards the door. He pictured his tired father coming home late and opening his schoolbag to leave these simple words of (32). His father never said “I love you”, but his love was hidden in every (33). His love might be silent, but it was always there, like a mountain.
Feeling a sudden rush of warmth, Peter picked up his pen again.

items.exp: 父亲寡言而忙碌，几乎不谈心，hardly。
渴望父亲陪伴，用 wished。

发现父亲鼓励的纸条，感到惊讶 surprised。

You can do it 是鼓励 encouragement。
便条藏在书里，父爱藏在每一页 page。

groups.label: A
groups.title: 给俱乐部起名
groups.passage:
Sunny Middle School — Student Learning Center — WEEKLY PROJECT
My Club, My Voice: Create a cool name for your favorite club.
Step 1 (Day 1): Think about your club. Decide what your club does. Drawing? Singing? Running? Reading?
Step 2 (Day 2): Mix words to make names. Rule: [fun word] + [thing you do] + club. Fun words: Bright, Happy, Green, Cool... Things you do: Singers, Runners, Readers, Helpers... For example, if your club is about reading, choose “Readers”.
Step 3 (Day 3—4): Draw a logo. Draw a picture for your favorite club. Write one short sentence to introduce the club.
Step 4 (Day 5): Share your work (5 minutes). Stand in front of the class. 1. Say your club name. 2. Say what you do. 3. Show your logo and introduce it. Vote for the most creative one.
Rules: Use English only (you can look up new words in a dictionary). Work in groups of four.

items.stem: What is the project for?
items.exp: 项目标题下写明为俱乐部起名字。

items.stem: How long does the project last?
items.exp: 步骤从 Day 1 到 Day 5，共五天。

items.stem: Which name follows the rule of Step 2?
items.exp: 按趣味词、活动者、club 的顺序。

items.stem: Which of the following activities is part of Step 4?
items.exp: 第四步包含展示并介绍标志。

items.stem: Where can you read the text?
items.exp: 页面有 Home、Projects 等导航，属于网站。

groups.label: B
groups.title: VR缓解疼痛
groups.passage: Every time Steve woke up, he felt his right hand was on fire. He could not lift a cup or touch cold water. The medicine he took didn’t work well. But one day, he put on a VR  headset and things began to change. VR treatment is being used in medical fields, especially for helping people with chronic  pain. In fact, VR can give people experiences that are similar to the real world. In a VR program, Steve was trying out a VR headset. Surprisingly, it took him to a different situation where he was able to move his right hand slowly. Jenny also received the VR treatment in this program. Her back pain bothered her for years. Wearing a VR headset, she was surprised to find she got a little better. So how does VR help? Scientists say that the pain is not only about the body. It also has something to do with the brain. When you fully focus on something exciting, your brain pays less attention to the pain. VR uses this idea to help people feel better. Of course, VR treatment may not suit everyone suffering from pain. It is still being studied, but for those living with pain every day, VR technology brings something important: hope.

items.stem: How does the writer start the text?
items.exp: 开头用 Steve 的疼痛经历举例。

items.stem: What did Steve do after putting on a VR headset?
items.exp: 第二段说他能缓慢移动右手。

items.stem: What does the underlined word “bothered” probably mean in Paragraph 2?
items.exp: 长期背痛困扰她，bothered 意为 troubled。

items.stem: How does VR make people feel less painful according to the text?
options: By making the brain focus less on pain.
By making the body stronger to fight pain.
By giving people medicine through the headset.
items.exp: 专注有趣体验时，大脑对疼痛关注更少。

items.stem: Which of the following ideas does the writer probably agree with?
options: VR treatment is suitable for everyone.
People pay little attention to VR treatment.
VR treatment can help people in some ways.
items.exp: 末段承认仍在研究，但能给患者希望。

groups.label: C
groups.title: 贝聿铭的建筑人生
groups.passage:
Ieoh Ming Pei was known as the master of modern architecture. He designed many famous buildings and landmarks around the world.
Pei was born in Guangzhou in 1917. He grew up in a family that valued education and traditional art. Suzhou was his ancestral hometown. Pei spent most of his childhood holidays there. During those holidays, he would visit the gardens whenever he had time. Seeing those rocks, stone bridges and waterfalls, he began to show interest in them. At the age of ten, Pei moved with his family to Shanghai. The city’s international architectural style had a strong influence on him. He decided to become an architect. In 1935, Pei went abroad to study. When he was 38, he started his company in New York. In 1983, he won the Pritzker Prize, the highest honor in architecture.
One of Pei’s most famous works is the glass pyramid in front of the Louvre Museum in Paris, which was designed in 1989. It showed his idea—let light design the buildings. Many people disliked it because it was so different from the traditional architecture at that time. But today, it is one of the most popular places in France. Suzhou Museum is another work of his. It opened in 2006 and became a must-go place later. Pei explained, “It should belong to Suzhou, but also to the world. It should be traditional, yet modern.” He left over 50 designs during his life.
Pei passed away in 2019 at the age of 102. His designs are regarded as the gifts to the world.

items.stem: Where did Pei begin to show interest in gardens?
items.exp: 在苏州度假参观园林时产生兴趣。

items.stem: What is the right order of the following facts according to Paragraph 2? ①He moved to Shanghai. ②He won the Pritzker Prize. ③He began to study abroad.
items.exp: 十岁搬上海、1935年留学、1983年获奖。

items.stem: What is the glass pyramid in front of the Louvre Museum like today?
items.exp: 如今玻璃金字塔是法国最受欢迎景点之一。

items.stem: What does Paragraph 3 mainly talk about?
items.exp: 第三段介绍卢浮宫金字塔、苏州博物馆等作品和成就。

items.stem: What can be the best title for the text?
items.exp: 文章围绕贝聿铭的建筑人生，C最贴切。

sections.title: 汾河的生态修复（六选五）
sections.passage:
Imagine you have just cleaned your classroom. Then a strict teacher in school walks in, looks around, and gives you a big smile. (49) But this time the testers are birds.
In recent years, groups of rare birds like black storks and egrets have been seen along the Fenhe River. (50) These birds are very picky: they only live near clean water. Their arrival makes the river full of life.
Things were quite different in the past. There were few rare birds. (51) Because the river was polluted seriously. Then the government started a plan to bring the river back to life. Workers spared no effort to turn dirty water into clean water. (52) These wetlands helped clean the water. The water quality has improved a lot.
(53) There are more plants growing in the wetlands. More and more birds choose the Fenhe River as their winter home.
When people take care of nature, nature gives back. The balance between humans and nature has become a reality in Shanxi.
choices: They rest along the river banks playing happily.
The results of people’s hard work are easy to see.
The Fenhe River is the mother river of Shanxi Province.
That is exactly what is happening along the Fenhe River.
What’s more, they cleaned and added wetlands along the river.

items.exp: 把教师检查清洁的比喻过渡到汾河生态。
They 承接稀有鸟类，描写它们在河岸休憩。
下句 Because 解释过去稀有鸟少的原因。
下句 These wetlands 承接清理和增加的湿地。
植物、鸟类增加是辛勤工作的成果。

sections.title: 理性消费与储蓄
sections.passage:
Money is part of our life. So we are faced with the same question: what to do with our money? Smart spending means using money in a way that fits real needs, real value and real plans.
In daily life, teenagers usually spend most of their money buying something necessary—food, clothes or school things. But sometimes, they buy things they don’t really need. Following the crowd may lead teenagers to buy something unnecessary. For example, when some classmates have the same kind of pencil case, a teenager may feel unhappy about having a different one. So he will buy a new one like theirs.
Teenagers can start learning how to manage money wisely at an early age. On Tom’s 6th birthday, his grandmother gave him several jars to help him make good use of money. One was for spending, one for saving and another for giving. It was at that time that Tom started his own money journal to record where the money had gone. He has had this habit since then.
Tom’s money journal: May 2nd: ¥18, a film ticket, remaining ¥82. May 9th: ¥25, a scarf for Mum, remaining ¥57. May 15th: ¥35, a dictionary, remaining ¥22. May 28th: ¥12, snacks and drinks, remaining ¥10.
Tom’s birthday present is more than several jars. His grandmother has given a kid the chance to learn lifelong values. The wider goal of the jars is to encourage teenagers to think more wisely about the money and the things they can do.
News: Xingfu Community Plants 8 Trees with Saved Money. This spring, Xingfu Community started a “Tree Bank” activity. Many teenagers took part in it. With their saved money, they bought 8 young trees. On Tree Planting Day, they planted the trees on a hill outside the city. “One coin can bring social meaning,” said a teenager.

items.stem: What does smart spending mean?
items.answer: It means using money in a way that fits real needs, real value and real plans.
items.exp: 第一段给出理性消费定义。

items.stem: What may lead teenagers to buy something unnecessary?
items.exp: 第二段说明盲目跟风导致非必要消费。

items.stem: Why did Tom’s grandmother give him several jars?
items.answer: To help him make good use of money.
items.exp: 奶奶希望他学会明智管理金钱。

items.stem: What were the top two things Tom spent money on in May?
items.answer: A dictionary and a scarf for Mum.
items.exp: 比较支出，字典35元、给妈妈的围巾25元最高。

items.stem: Will you give away money like the teenagers in Xingfu Community? Why or why not?
items.answer: Yes, I will. Because the world will be a better place to live in if everyone does something good for society.
items.exp: 开放题，要表态并给出合理的个人或社会理由。

sections.title: 提高记忆力
sections.passage:
How to improve memory
You may find it hard to remember what you have learned in class. In fact, it’s quite common to (59) things. Here is some advice.
You can use songs to help you. Pick a song (60) interests you. Change what you need to remember into its lyrics. Then you can memorize them as you sing. It is relaxing and easy.
A mind map helps you organize information in a visual way. We need several steps to create a mind map. First, write the main idea in the center. For example, write “(61)” in the center. Then, write other key ideas around the main idea like “the Mid-Autumn Festival”, “the Spring Festival”, “the Dragon Boat Festival” and so on. Next, write more words about the key ideas like “date”, “food”, “activities” and so on. Now, look (62) the mind map. It’s very helpful, right?
原图文字：中心词 festivals；分支为 the Mid-Autumn Festival、the Spring Festival、the Dragon Boat Festival 等；Dragon Boat Festival 再分出 date、food、activities。
No one can remember everything, (63) everybody can learn how to improve their memory. Follow the tips, and you will make progress.

修饰先行词 song 的定语从句用 that 或 which。

sections.title: 游晋祠博物馆
sections.passage:
词库：I / run / luck / tell / share / clear / see / old / idea / move / visit / decide
I am a British student studying history at Shanxi University. Last Sunday, I (64) Jinci Museum. It was a trip that I had planned for a long time.
After stepping inside, I saw a wooden building stand in front of me. I (65) by a local guide that it was the Shuijing Stage, an old theater dating back to the Ming and Qing Dynasties. When an opera singer sang on the stage, everyone in the yard could hear the voice (66). I looked closely at its wooden structure. There were no modern machines, just hands and clever (67) from ancient builders. The wisdom and creativity of Chinese people surprised (68) a lot.
What also caught my attention was the ancient trees. The guide told me that one of them, the Zhou Cypress, was planted during the Western Zhou Dynasty. It was much (69) than I had ever imagined. Watching its dark green leaves dancing in the wind, I found myself lost in its beauty. I felt (70) to have the chance to go there. It was an unforgettable experience, which made me fall in love with Chinese culture. I made a (71) to go to more places of interest in Shanxi.
Now I understand why people say, “If you want (72) thousands of years of Chinese civilization, you should come to Shanxi.” I (73) the experience with my friends when I return to my hometown next month. The history of Shanxi is more than just stories of the past. It is also a cultural treasure.

我被导游告知，用过去时被动语态 was told。

sections.prompt: 以 A small step, a big breakthrough 为题写不少于80词演讲稿，包含：你眼中的小步是什么；一次迈出小步的亲身经历；经历对你的影响。不出现真实人名、校名。开头：Hello, everyone! 结尾：That’s all. Thank you!
sections.sample:
Hello, everyone! In my eyes, small steps are the effort to learn something new and the courage to put up my hand in class. These small steps bring out the best in me.
I still remember working out a problem quickly in a math class. However, afraid of making a mistake, I hid my hands under the desk. Just then, I caught the teacher’s encouraging look. Taking a deep breath, I slowly raised my hand. My voice shook at first, but as I explained the steps clearly, my fear gradually disappeared. It was through this small step that I made a breakthrough.
Not only do I feel more confident now, but I can also face challenges bravely. Remember: take one small step today, and you will see yourself grow. That’s all. Thank you!
sections.exp: 先定义小步，再用具体经历说明突破，最后写影响。范文来自附卷答案。
